column8: Tue 17 Nov: store only; the standing pre-award guarantee is about conduct, not money, so it serves no part beyond showing who stands behind a host's word.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the buyer sets the guarantee list edition by edition, while Laura's test (money she already owns, IPS l.15) is set once; row 8 shows the list bends.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d store, the host's open shape (G 4.1, no cap in the annex wording) that her figure refuses; one line of row 43 and the contrast behind row 5, read at source.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d store; someone must underwrite the village's overrun, while Laura's stated figure underwrites none and her flexibility may meet one because it is promised to no one (IPS l.15, SKELETON 3d).

Tue 17 Nov: 3d team lead-in, the best row: Rule 36.2 makes the fixed-figure party immune to overruns; fix the use: her stated figure has the IOC's shape, but she is also the founder who may meet overruns from her flexibility (3b: owners pay overruns; Q11e), so never imply she never pays one; travels with SKELETON 3d's clause.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d, the second half of row 5's clause: the IOC's own fixed figure is an estimated value and its broadcast part can be cut if revenue does not arrive (the anticipated-receipts point of Q43), while hers is held after the move.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d store for what is never asked: joint and several liability makes each signer answer for all; Laura's figure is hers alone and asks no one to stand behind it.
Tue 17 Nov: 3c store beside Q43's precedent: since 2019 some host guarantees may arrive up to 18 months after the vote; Laura states no figure before the move, so no grace period is needed.
Tue 17 Nov: store; a partner that shares the surplus and none of the deficit; Laura's cap sends anything above her top to her flexibility (3b); Keel reading of two documents, said as such.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the Charter moved all money risk to the host between 1975 and 1993; after Montreal only as dates, never as the cause, which no IOC text read states.
Tue 17 Nov: store; the 1996 Charter let a guarantee rest on third parties' money; the citations are right: IPS l.11 for the ten payments, l.15 for the stated figure.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; drop 'the Olympic cousin of Laura's owned ends': a small yearly good-faith deposit forfeited on cancellation is not the money behind a stated figure, as the row's own disanalogy says.

Tue 17 Nov: the card itself says row 15 supersedes this 2012 measure; its use, one clause in 3b, would set the Games beside her flexibility, which the facility's out-of-scope cost forbids (case l.164).

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d contrast between a guaranteed budget and her capped top; say a starting point for spending, not a floor, since the floor names the Treasury fund bought in January 2028; causation untested in the 2012 paper.

Tue 17 Nov: support for row 17 only (10 of 10 overran, 0% schedule overrun, in their data); the 172% mean never in 3b or beside her flexibility as a size for overruns (facility cost out of scope, case l.164; Q5d holds the small-building class); cite with row 20's counter-study.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse the use: it reads the Games' fat tail as the tail of her building's overruns, the yardstick the case rules out (l.164) and the row's own disanalogy breaks; the sizing point (half the shares, not a cost) is already IPS l.15 and SKELETON 3e area (5).

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3c aha from another field: a date that cannot move turns every problem into money, so fixed payment dates need the money fixed before them (IPS l.13); the store's sequence-risk point (H2-006) told from megaprojects; payment dates, never her building's deadline.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the host's question is whether it can absorb the tail, and Laura never promises the tail; never apply the 20% three-fold heuristic to her building.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3b shape: the reform asks the fixed-figure party to share overruns, while Laura keeps her figure fixed and her flexibility outside it; never set London's 4.3% contingency beside her flexibility.

Tue 17 Nov: guard on rows 15 and 17 wherever an Olympic figure appears, not a 3b clause (no Olympic figure goes in 3b); never say the Games caused Greece's crisis; abstract only, so read the method before citing.
Tue 17 Nov: store guard: the Oxford figures moved between 2012 and 2021, so any figure used cites the 2021 paper and one number; not checked line by line.
Tue 17 Nov: store; Montreal's figure had nothing held behind it and others paid for thirty years (official report, CBC); a public megaproject in 1970s inflation, never a guide to her building.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3c-3d colour for the case's own warning (l.114: promising more than she can give damages credibility); quote as reported by CBC and the Gazette, no primary read; never a guard on Treasury words (Book 19).

Tue 17 Nov: 3d aha: the organisers' own report called the Games self-financing once the buildings were left out; Laura's words state only her own figure and where the facility's total will be set, never that the facility is paid for; the organisers' defence, not an audit.

Tue 17 Nov: store; the IOC's own lesson (funding in place beforehand) beside Q43; a variety of sources means others' money, which her stated figure never uses (IPS l.15); search extract only, re-read before citing.
Tue 17 Nov: store for 3d's what is never asked; the guarantee moved to the USOC and the surplus came from TV and sponsors, so never refusing guarantees makes money.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; UNVERIFIED, Killanin's 1978 letter read through a dissertation; read the archive before any use.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (3) store beside Q92 (her own money needs no vote): Denver's Games ended when voters barred public money; a ballot, not a market, and never a forecast of any vote.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d contrast: an unknown sum on an unread contract against a known figure she already owns, stated once after the move.

Tue 17 Nov: store; the sharper parallel is 3a's test (hoped-for income counted at nothing) and Q90's pledge discounts, not her own figure, which holds no co-sponsor money by definition; KSG review read through a newspaper; the cap disputed.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e or 2.3 aha: Rio's state promise broke when its own income fell in the downturn the bills came due, IPS l.9's mechanism on a government's books; Brazil only, never beside Taiwan's public co-sponsors, who fall short through budget votes, not recessions (Q10d, CANON B4); can, never together.

Tue 17 Nov: store only; fix 'nothing is owed after 2033 beyond her own figure': the ten payments run to 2042, each owned in Treasuries, so say her facility figure is the only facility sum she states and it is held.
Tue 17 Nov: store guard: overruns land on the guarantor; BBC 2004 and IOBE 2015 measure different things, and never the Olympics caused the crisis.
Tue 17 Nov: store for 3d: the one case found where missing funding guarantees counted against a bid; causation not shown (public support differed); say funded, avoid signed beside the ink image.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d store: an honest guarantee never called, yet public money paid outside the budget, so Laura's words say what her figure covers and where the facility's total is set (SKELETON 3d).

Tue 17 Nov: 3d store, the capped tier of row 43: a dollar cap with a waterfall of who pays first; her figure has no layer behind it to call on; bill text via a council-file copy, signature of the support contract unconfirmed.
Tue 17 Nov: the same LA28 waterfall as row 36; the contingency built from future revenue and the negotiator's quote travel with it.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; answers the card's Expo half (a government guarantee and a financial plan, not money held); BIE procedure rules not read.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; the US reservation guarantees only its own obligations; a treaty point on legal power, close to trivia for the report.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d at most; fix the echo: France's test keeps the project's risk off others' money, while IPS l.11 keeps the ten payments from resting on others' money (a mirror, not a match), and any facility figure cites l.15.
Tue 17 Nov: store only; Hannover's guarantees ended at the guarantors and business shared ownership but not losses (opposition wording); 45% of planned visits is Keel arithmetic.

Tue 17 Nov: 3d aha with H7-086 (fixed dollars, never a share): Osaka's partners each promised a third, so each bill rose about 1.9 times, while a dollar figure like hers does not rise with overruns; Japanese public partners, never a guide to her building's cost.

Tue 17 Nov: 3c or 3d store, the four-shape comparison; row 5 is the one-clause form that fits 3d's budget, so four lines only in an exhibit-free sentence if room; synthesis is Keel's on rows read at source.

Tue 17 Nov: refuse: the blank-cheque turn makes ink a signature, the reading the conceit's definition (owned, card Q42, V2.4 guard 7) was written to exclude, as Q106-031 was refused; 3d already holds the seal turn.
